metric.semantic_determinacy.basis: all-44-probes (fixed capability universe); this metric is computed over the frozen probe set independent of FULL/PARTIAL/NONE support level per spec 6.1.3.B, since branching is measured on whatever local surface form exists for the language, including substituted/PARTIAL forms named by R9.
metric.semantic_determinacy.limitations: This is a single-language (Swift) shard. Cross-language comparability of the reported 0-100 score depends on every other language shard applying the identical cap (log2(8)=3) and formula; that invariant is recorded here for the runner's aggregation/audit step.
metric.semantic_determinacy.methodology_note: Per spec 6.1.3.B, raw value is the branching count B_i (materially distinct interpretations compatible with the local surface form alone, before consulting external declarations) for each of the 44 frozen probes, reduced to mean(log2(B_i)). Lower branching is better. This shard covers only Swift. Normalization to 0-100 (100=best/most determinate) uses score = 100 * clamp(1 - mean_log2B / log2(8), 0, 1); the cap log2(8)=3 is drawn from the probe set's own worst-case enumerated outcome family (F05.P1 enumerates up to 6 materially distinct call-site aliasing/mutation outcomes, rounded up to the next power of two, 8, as the documented ceiling for a single probe's branching in this universe). This normalization constant is recorded here for audit and must be applied identically to every language shard measuring this metric so cross-shard aggregation is comparable.

F01.P1.rationale: `let n = 7` is an immutable local value binding with inferred Int type; local form alone is fully determinate (value semantics, immutability, initialization all explicit via `let`).

F01.P2.rationale: `var counter: Int64 = 0` vs `let LIMIT: Int64 = 100` mark mutability unambiguously via keyword choice.

F02.P1.rationale: Swift's definite-initialization analysis is a local, syntactic, deterministic check over the two-way branch; no external lookup changes the reader's conclusion.

F02.P2.rationale: Swift has no zero-cost 'declared but contents unspecified' array literal; the substituted fragment (Array(repeating:count:) or UnsafeMutablePointer.allocate) states its initialization state explicitly and locally.

F03.P1.rationale: `x += 1` on Int32 traps on overflow by Swift's default (checked) arithmetic; behavior is fixed by the operator alone.

F03.P2.rationale: `xs[1] = 42` on an Array bound by `xs` mutates that binding's storage; Swift's value/COW semantics make this locally determinate.

F04.P1.rationale: Swift has no first-class second name aliasing a stack scalar in the same scope; the only standard mechanisms (withUnsafeMutablePointer closure scope vs a class-boxed alias) diverge in whether the alias outlives the call, so two materially different lifetime/aliasing readings remain locally compatible.

F04.P2.rationale: `let window = xs[1...]` (ArraySlice) with `let` fixes non-mutability of the binding and Swift's documented COW slicing guarantees no eager copy.

F04.P3.rationale: `===` is Swift's dedicated reference-identity operator, unambiguous from local form.

F05.P1.rationale: The bare call site `f(x)` does not disclose, without consulting f's parameter type, whether x's element type is a value type (fully copied, no caller-visible effect) or a class/reference type (full aliasing); two materially distinct outcome families remain compatible with the call-site syntax alone.

F05.P2.rationale: Swift's `inout` parameter and `&cell` call-site marker jointly and unambiguously declare writable-alias passing.

F05.P3.rationale: Swift closures capture enclosing locals by reference to the captured variable by default; declared closure syntax is locally determinate.

F06.P1.rationale: Returning an Int element (value type) from `mid` is independent of the source array by Swift's value semantics; no aliasing ambiguity remains.

F06.P2.rationale: Tuple return `(Int, Int)` with tuple-destructuring `let (q, r) = ...` is fully determinate.

F07.P1.rationale: `a * b + c` on Int32 traps on overflow deterministically; standard precedence applies.

F07.P2.rationale: Swift integer division truncates toward zero and `%` follows the dividend's sign; both are fixed language rules, not dependent on external context.

F08.P1.rationale: Using `addingReportingOverflow` (rung i) makes the overflow outcome an explicit, locally visible tuple result.

F08.P2.rationale: An explicit local `b == 0` guard makes the zero-divisor outcome fully determinate at the site.

F09.P1.rationale: Swift's `==` on String is documented to compare Unicode-canonical content equality, not identity; fixed by the operator/type pair alone.

F09.P2.rationale: `xs.sorted(by: >)` explicitly returns a new array (non-mutating) per Swift's documented value-semantics API naming convention (non-`sort` name implies new array).

F10.P1.rationale: `Int32(exactly: big)` is Swift's explicit checked/optional-returning conversion; local form fixes the out-of-range outcome as nil.

F10.P2.rationale: Swift requires an explicit `Double(i)` conversion before mixed arithmetic; there is no silent implicit promotion, so the site is fully determinate.

F11.P1.rationale: `xs[i]` traps on out-of-range by fixed Array subscript semantics.

F11.P2.rationale: `xs[1..<4]` (ArraySlice) shares storage under Swift's documented COW slicing rule.

F12.P1.rationale: Optional<Int32> and the `??` coalescing operator are both explicit, fixed-semantics constructs.

F12.P2.rationale: `o.map(h)` on Optional is documented to short-circuit on nil without evaluating h; fully determinate.

F13.P1.rationale: `throws` in the declared signature plus `try` propagation at the call site make failure and propagation locally explicit.

F13.P2.rationale: `do { try ... } catch { ... }` bounds the protected region explicitly and locally.

F14.P1.rationale: Swift `enum` is closed by language rule; no external declaration can add a case.

F14.P2.rationale: `switch` over an enum without `default` is exhaustiveness-checked at compile time by the compiler; the local form itself signals this guarantee (a non-exhaustive switch fails to compile).

F14.P3.rationale: Protocol conformance added in a separate file/module and dispatched through an existential/generic can resolve via static (witness-table) or dynamic (@objc/vtable) dispatch depending on how the abstract type is used; the bare call-through-abstraction site does not by itself disambiguate which dispatch mechanism Swift selects.

F15.P1.rationale: `func head<T>(_ xs: [T]) -> T` states the parametric relationship between argument and result type directly in the declaration.

F15.P2.rationale: `func max_of<T: Comparable>(...)` states the constraint at the declaration; misuse is diagnosed there, not at instantiation.

F15.P3.rationale: `[any Named]` (or `[Named]` protocol-typed array) with dynamic dispatch to `.tag()` is a fixed, documented existential-dispatch mechanism.

F16.P1.rationale: `xs.reduce(0, +)` is a standard, fixed-semantics fold; no ambiguity.

F16.P2.rationale: Swift's Dictionary iteration order is explicitly documented as unspecified/unstable across executions, so the local construct itself is compatible with more than one materially different traversal-order outcome (though the lookup-miss default via `mp["b", default: 0]` is itself determinate).

F17.P1.rationale: `defer` placed immediately after acquisition fixes the release point locally and covers every exit path including thrown errors.

F17.P2.rationale: `deinit` on a non-reference-cycle class value is deterministic under ARC given a single, non-escaping owner in the local block, matching the probe's construction.

F18.P1.rationale: `import Foundation` (or no import for `print`) plus `print("x")` is fixed, standard-library-documented behavior.

F18.P2.rationale: `public`/`internal` (default) access modifiers are explicit, fixed-meaning keywords enforced by the compiler across module boundaries.

F19.P1.rationale: `async let` / `Task {}` plus `await` produces a single documented join semantics; although the two child tasks may execute on arbitrary threads, the combining read after both awaits is deterministic given no shared mutable state in the probe.

F19.P2.rationale: An `actor`-isolated counter serializes all increments by Swift's documented actor-isolation guarantee, making the race-freedom locally determinate from the `actor` keyword.

F20.P1.rationale: Calling imported C `abs(_:)` via the platform module (Glibc/Darwin) uses Swift's fixed, documented C-interop calling convention.

F20.P2.rationale: `@_cdecl("add2")` is Swift's documented (if underscored/compiler-internal) mechanism for a stable, unmangled, C-ABI exported symbol; its effect is fixed by the attribute itself.
